P2600.title: Coolant Pump A Control Circuit / Open
P2600.description: The controller cannot drive the electric coolant pump A control line. Without circulation, engine and aftertreatment can overheat or warm up incorrectly.

causes.label: Open pump motor winding
Broken control wire to the pump

P2601.title: Coolant Pump A Control Circuit Performance/Stuck Off
P2601.description: The electric coolant pump A is commanded on but does not run. Coolant temperature climbs faster than expected with no flow detected.

causes.label: Pump motor seized by debris or sediment
Cracked rotor magnet decouples drive
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2602.title: Coolant Pump A Control Circuit Low
P2602.description: P2602 reports that the control circuit of electric coolant pump A reads low - a short to ground, or a corresponding report from the driver stage. Which pump is A varies: Ford's 2020-2023 gasoline OBD summary defines it as the auxiliary pump of the high-temperature loop for cabin heating, checked continuously over 5 s above 11 V; GM's 2008 3.6 L LLT table uses an after-run pump (P2602 = circuit to ground, stored only as pending code without warning light). VW's 2014 books set it below about 3.0 V on the Passat and CC and below 2.8-3.2 V on the Touareg. P2600 is the open circuit, P2601 the performance fault, P2603 the high-side fault. Without the pump, heater output or after-run cooling of a hot engine may suffer.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to ground
Internal fault in the electric coolant pump or its electronics
Coolant or water ingress into the pump connector

symptoms: Fault code stored; warning light depends on manufacturer (none at GM)
Weak cabin heating
No after-run of the pump after a hot shutdown

P2603.title: Coolant Pump A Control Circuit High
P2603.description: P2603 means the control circuit of electric coolant pump A reads high - typically a short to battery voltage, or an overcurrent seen by the driver stage. Ford's 2020-2023 gasoline OBD summary assigns pump A to the auxiliary high-temperature loop for cabin heating and sets P2602/P2603 when the smart driver reports a fault within 5 s. GM's 2008 3.6 L LLT table monitors its after-run pump for a circuit fault to voltage (pending code only, no warning light). VW's 2014 books use a current threshold: about 0.60-1.20 A on the Passat and CC, 5.5-10 A on the Touareg. CARB requires output components to be checked for circuit faults. P2600 is the open circuit, P2601 performance, P2602 the low-side fault. Heater output or after-run cooling may be lost.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to battery voltage
Seized or sluggish pump drawing excessive current
Faulty driver stage in the ECM

symptoms: Fault code stored; warning light depends on manufacturer (none at GM)
Weak cabin heating
Higher coolant temperature after hot shutdown

P2604.title: Intake Air Heater A Circuit Range/Performance
P2604.description: P2604 is the functional check of intake air heater A - the grid heater in the intake that warms the charge air of a diesel engine for cold starts. The circuit responds, but current, voltage drop or heating effect do not match the command. CARB requires glow plugs and intake air heaters to be monitored for proper functional response and for correct current and voltage drop. Volvo's heavy-truck engine bulletins (2020, 2022) list P2604-7F among the codes caused by a weak pre-heat relay and fix it with a software update, a check of terminal tension at heater and relay, and a new relay plus supply cable. P0540-P0543 cover the electrical faults of heater A, P2605-P2608 heater B, P2609 the system. Expect hard cold starts and white smoke.

causes.label: Worn or sticking intake air heater relay
Loose or burnt terminals on the heater supply cable
Degraded or partly open heater grid
Outdated engine software (manufacturer update available)

symptoms: Hard starting in cold weather
White smoke and rough running after a cold start
Check engine light

P2605.title: Intake Air Heater B Circuit / Open
P2605.description: The controller cannot drive the secondary intake air heater (heater grid B) used on diesel engines for cold-start support. The grid stays cold so cold-start emissions and white smoke increase.

causes.label: Open heater grid element
Failed heater relay or open coil

P2606.title: Intake Air Heater B Circuit Range/Performance
P2606.description: The secondary intake air heater current does not match expected resistance. Either the grid is partially open or the relay contacts have high resistance.

causes.label: Partial element failure raises grid resistance
Burned relay contacts
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2607.title: Intake Air Heater B Circuit Low
P2607.description: Voltage on the secondary intake air heater control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted relay coil.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in relay coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2608.title: Intake Air Heater B Circuit High
P2608.description: Voltage on the secondary intake air heater control line is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open relay coil.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to a B+ supply
Open relay coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2609.title: Intake Air Heater System Performance
P2609.description: The intake air heater system did not raise intake temperature by the expected amount during cold-start support. Suggests low current draw, poor connection to the grid, or a failed temperature feedback path.

causes.label: High-resistance battery feed to the heater
Intake air temperature sensor reads with offset

P260A.title: PTO Control Circuit / Open
P260A.description: The controller cannot drive the power take-off (PTO) engagement line on commercial vehicles. The PTO will not engage even when commanded by the body controller or operator switch.

causes.label: Open coil in the PTO engagement solenoid
Broken wire to the PTO solenoid

P260B.title: PTO Control Circuit Low
P260B.description: Voltage on the PTO engagement control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted solenoid coil.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in the solenoid coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P260C.title: PTO Control Circuit High
P260C.description: Voltage on the PTO engagement control line is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open solenoid coil.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to a B+ supply
Open solenoid coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P260D.title: PTO Engaged Lamp Control Circuit
P260D.description: The dashboard PTO engaged lamp control circuit is faulty. Driver may not see whether the PTO is currently driving an external accessory.

causes.label: Burnt-out indicator bulb
Open or shorted wire between cluster and ECU

P260E.title: Particulate Filter Regeneration Lamp Control Circuit
P260E.description: The DPF regeneration warning lamp circuit is faulty. The driver may not be alerted to a required highway run that supports passive regeneration.

causes.label: Burnt-out indicator bulb
Open or shorted wire to the cluster

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on
Power loss / limp mode
Increased fuel consumption
Failed forced regeneration attempts

P260F.title: EVAP System Monitoring Processor Performance
P260F.description: The dedicated EVAP monitoring processor (often a small auxiliary CPU inside the engine controller or a separate module) does not pass its self-test or runs out of step with the main monitor logic.

causes.label: Internal fault in the monitoring processor
Software memory corruption
Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

symptoms: Check engine light on
Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay
Failed emissions inspection
Loose-cap warning may appear

P2610.title: ECM/PCM Internal Engine Off Timer Performance
P2610.description: The engine controller's internal soak-time/engine-off timer fails its plausibility check — for example readings claim instant cool-down or never-cooled. Cold-start enrichment, EVAP and catalyst monitors depend on this timer; a fault freezes those readiness monitors.

causes.label: ECU internal timer fault
Keep-alive memory power intermittent

P2611.title: A/C Refrigerant Distribution Valve A Control Circuit / Open
P2611.description: The A/C refrigerant distribution valve A (used to switch refrigerant flow between front and rear evaporators or between cabin and battery cooling on EVs) cannot be driven by the controller.

causes.label: Open coil in the valve solenoid
Broken control wire

P2612.title: A/C Refrigerant Distribution Valve A Control Circuit Low
P2612.description: Voltage on the A/C distribution valve A control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted solenoid coil.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in the valve solenoid
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2613.title: A/C Refrigerant Distribution Valve A Control Circuit High
P2613.description: Voltage on the A/C distribution valve A control line is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open solenoid coil.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to a B+ supply
Open solenoid coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2614.title: Camshaft Position Output Circuit/Open
P2614.description: The camshaft position output signal sent from the ECU to other modules is interrupted. Other systems that rely on the cam reference (e.g. transmission, hybrid module) do not receive a valid signal.

causes.label: Open output wiring
Internal ECU output driver fault
Pin pushed back out of connector body

symptoms: Check engine light on
Power loss especially in mid-rpm range
Possible rough idle or stalling
Increased fuel consumption

P2615.title: Camshaft A Position Signal Output Circuit Low Bank 1
P2615.description: The buffered camshaft A position output that the engine controller sends to other modules (transmission, body, ignition module) is below the expected level on bank 1. Other modules cannot use the cam phase reference for synchronisation.

causes.label: Output wire shorted to ground
Output buffer transistor failed
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Check engine light on
Power loss especially in mid-rpm range
Possible rough idle or stalling
Increased fuel consumption

P2616.title: Camshaft A Position Signal Output Circuit High Bank 1
P2616.description: The buffered camshaft A position output is above the expected level on bank 1. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open output stage.

causes.label: Output wire shorted to B+
Output buffer open
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Check engine light on
Power loss especially in mid-rpm range
Possible rough idle or stalling
Increased fuel consumption

P2617.title: Crankshaft Position Signal Output Circuit / Open
P2617.description: The buffered crankshaft position output that the engine controller sends to ignition modules and the transmission cannot drive its line. Open detected on the output side.

causes.label: Open wire between ECU and downstream module
Output buffer internally open

P2618.title: Crankshaft Position Signal Output Circuit Low
P2618.description: The buffered crankshaft position output is below the expected level. Usually a short to ground on the output line or a failed buffer.

causes.label: Output wire shorted to ground
Buffer transistor failed
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2619.title: Crankshaft Position Signal Output Circuit High
P2619.description: The buffered crankshaft position output is above the expected level. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open output stage.

causes.label: Output wire shorted to B+
Output buffer open
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P261A.title: Coolant Pump B Control Circuit / Open
P261A.description: The controller cannot drive the second electric coolant pump (B). Often used for aftertreatment, turbo cool-down, or hybrid battery loops — fault stops circulation in that loop.

causes.label: Open pump motor winding
Broken control wire to the pump

P261B.title: Coolant Pump B Control Circuit Performance/Stuck Off
P261B.description: The second electric coolant pump is commanded on but does not run. Cooling demand of the connected loop is not satisfied.

causes.label: Pump motor seized by sediment
Cracked rotor magnet decouples drive
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P261C.title: Coolant Pump B Control Circuit Low
P261C.description: Voltage on the second coolant pump control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted motor winding.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to ground
Motor winding short
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P261D.title: Coolant Pump B Control Circuit High
P261D.description: Voltage on the second coolant pump control line is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open motor winding.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to B+
Open motor winding
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P261E.title: Coolant Pump B Control Circuit Stuck On
P261E.description: The second coolant pump runs even when no command is active. Driver is stuck on or the wire is shorted to a permanent supply.

causes.label: ECU output driver stuck on
Control wire shorted to a permanent B+ supply
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P261F.title: Coolant Pump A Control Circuit Stuck On
P261F.description: The first coolant pump runs even when no command is active. Driver is stuck on or the wire is shorted to a permanent supply.

causes.label: ECU output driver stuck on
Control wire shorted to a permanent B+ supply
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2620.title: Throttle Position Output Circuit
P2620.description: A general electrical fault on the ECU output that broadcasts the throttle position signal to other modules — for example to the transmission control or hybrid drive controller.

causes.label: Output wire open or shorted
ECU output stage failed

symptoms: Check engine light on
Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Hesitation or surging
Idle too high or too low

P2621.title: Throttle Position Output Circuit Low
P2621.description: The buffered throttle position output that the engine controller sends to the transmission and body modules is below the expected level. Usually a short to ground or a failed output stage.

causes.label: Output wire shorted to ground
Output buffer transistor failed
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Check engine light on
Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Hesitation or surging
Idle too high or too low

P2622.title: Throttle Position Output Circuit High
P2622.description: The buffered throttle position output is above the expected level. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open output stage.

causes.label: Output wire shorted to B+
Output buffer open
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Check engine light on
Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Hesitation or surging
Idle too high or too low

P2623.title: Injector Control Pressure Regulator Circuit / Open
P2623.description: The Injector Control Pressure (ICP) regulator on hydraulically actuated injectors (HEUI diesel) or the high-pressure regulator on common-rail systems cannot be driven. Injection pressure cannot be controlled, engine may not start.

causes.label: Open coil in the pressure regulator
Broken control wire

P2624.title: Injector Control Pressure Regulator Circuit Low
P2624.description: Voltage on the ICP regulator control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted regulator coil.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in regulator coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2625.title: Injector Control Pressure Regulator Circuit High
P2625.description: Voltage on the ICP regulator control line is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open regulator coil.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to B+
Open regulator coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2626.title: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Trim Circuit/Open Bank 1 Sensor 1
P2626.description: The ECU detects an open in the pumping current trim circuit of the wide-band oxygen sensor on bank 1 sensor 1. Without trim correction, the lambda value reported by the sensor is not accurate.

causes.label: Trim wire open
Internal sensor fault
Pin pushed back out of connector body

symptoms: Check engine light on
Increased fuel consumption
Possible rough idle or hesitation
Failed emissions test

P2627.title: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Trim Circuit Low Bank 1 Sensor 1
P2627.description: On a wide-band (broadband) O2 sensor, the trim resistor circuit that calibrates the pumping current is reading low on bank 1 sensor 1. Air-fuel feedback gain is wrong, causing rich or lean offsets.

causes.label: Short in the calibration trim resistor
Water intrusion in the sensor connector
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Check engine light on
Increased fuel consumption
Possible rough idle or hesitation
Failed emissions test

P2628.title: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Trim Circuit High Bank 1 Sensor 1
P2628.description: The wide-band trim resistor circuit on bank 1 sensor 1 reads high. Air-fuel feedback gain is wrong, causing offsets that the controller cannot compensate.

causes.label: Open calibration trim resistor
Corroded sensor connector
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Check engine light on
Increased fuel consumption
Possible rough idle or hesitation
Failed emissions test

P2629.title: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Trim Circuit / Open Bank 2 Sensor 1
P2629.description: The wide-band trim resistor circuit on bank 2 sensor 1 is open. Air-fuel feedback for bank 2 cannot be calibrated, fuel control runs degraded.

causes.label: Open calibration trim resistor
Open sensor connector pin

symptoms: Check engine light on
Increased fuel consumption
Possible rough idle or hesitation
Failed emissions test

P262A.title: Fuel Injector - Pilot Injection Not Learned
P262A.description: The pilot (pre) injection learning routine on a common-rail diesel did not complete successfully. Without learned pilot quantity, combustion noise increases and NOx may rise.

causes.label: Injector flow drift outside learning window
Unstable rail pressure during learning cycle

symptoms: Check engine light on
Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Increased fuel consumption
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

P262B.title: Control Module Power Off Timer Performance
P262B.description: The internal power-down timer of the engine controller does not run as expected. The module either stays awake too long after key-off (battery drain) or shuts down too early (no aftertreatment cool-down or learn-write).

causes.label: Intermittent main relay opens early
Software timer counter corrupted

P262C.title: Sensor Reference Voltage G Circuit / Open
P262C.description: The 5 V reference G output that the engine controller supplies to a group of sensors is open. All sensors fed from this rail will report invalid readings.

causes.label: Open wire on the reference rail
Open inside the ECU reference output

P262D.title: Sensor Reference Voltage G Circuit Low
P262D.description: The 5 V reference G voltage is below the expected level. Usually a short to ground or excessive load from a downstream sensor pulling the rail down.

causes.label: Reference wire shorted to ground
Sensor on the rail shorted internally to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P262E.title: Sensor Reference Voltage G Circuit High
P262E.description: The 5 V reference G voltage is above the expected level. Typical causes are a short to battery or an internal regulator failure.

causes.label: Reference wire shorted to a B+ supply
Internal 5 V regulator failed
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P262F.title: Sensor Reference Voltage G Circuit Range/Performance
P262F.description: The 5 V reference G voltage is within range but unstable or offset against expected. Loose ground or marginal regulator load.

causes.label: High-resistance ground for the reference rail
One sensor draws excessive current and shifts the rail
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2630.title: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Trim Circuit Low Bank 2 Sensor 1
P2630.description: The wide-band trim resistor circuit on bank 2 sensor 1 reads low. Air-fuel feedback gain on bank 2 is wrong, causing rich or lean offsets.

causes.label: Short in the calibration trim resistor
Water intrusion in the sensor connector
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Check engine light on
Increased fuel consumption
Possible rough idle or hesitation
Failed emissions test

P2631.title: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Trim Circuit High Bank 2 Sensor 1
P2631.description: The wide-band trim resistor circuit on bank 2 sensor 1 reads high. Air-fuel feedback gain on bank 2 is wrong, the controller cannot compensate the offset.

causes.label: Open calibration trim resistor
Corroded sensor connector
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Check engine light on
Increased fuel consumption
Possible rough idle or hesitation
Failed emissions test

P2632.title: Fuel Pump B Control Circuit / Open
P2632.description: The controller cannot drive the secondary fuel pump (B). Common on dual-tank trucks, GDI lift-pump systems, or alt-fuel installations — fault stops fuel delivery from this stage.

causes.label: Open pump motor winding
Failed pump relay

symptoms: Check engine light on
Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm
Possible long cranking time

P2633.title: Fuel Pump B Control Circuit Low
P2633.description: Voltage on the second fuel pump control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted motor winding.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in pump motor
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Check engine light on
Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm
Possible long cranking time

P2634.title: Fuel Pump B Control Circuit High
P2634.description: Voltage on the second fuel pump control line is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open motor winding.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to B+
Open motor winding
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Check engine light on
Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm
Possible long cranking time

P2635.title: Fuel Pump A Low Flow / Performance
P2635.description: The ECU detects insufficient fuel flow from fuel pump A. Either the pump is worn out, the supply line is restricted, or the pressure regulator does not allow proper flow.

causes.label: Worn fuel pump
Clogged fuel filter
Pressure regulator fault

symptoms: Check engine light on
Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm
Possible long cranking time

P2636.title: Fuel Pump B Low Flow/Performance
P2636.description: The second fuel pump runs but does not deliver expected volume or pressure. Worn pump, restricted filter, or leaking pressure regulator.

causes.label: Worn impeller reduces volumetric efficiency
Restricted in-tank or in-line fuel filter
Pressure regulator leaks back to tank

symptoms: Check engine light on
Hard start, no start, or stalling under load
Power loss especially at high load or rpm
Possible long cranking time

P2637.title: Torque Management Feedback Signal A
P2637.description: The torque feedback signal A from the transmission or other torque user is missing or invalid. The engine controller cannot reduce torque on shift requests, which can cause harsh shifts.

causes.label: Required CAN message not received in time
Source module reports an internal fault

P2638.title: Torque Management Feedback Signal A Range/Performance
P2638.description: The torque feedback signal A is present but its value is implausible against measured engine load and speed. Sender calibration or sensor offset is suspected.

causes.label: Sender calibration drift
Bus value corrupted by EMI
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2639.title: Torque Management Feedback Signal A Low
P2639.description: The torque feedback signal A reads below its valid range. Either the source reports a value below physical possibility or the bus signal is stuck low.

causes.label: Source module sends invalid low value
Signal stuck low on the bus

P263A.title: MIL Control Circuit Low
P263A.description: Voltage on the malfunction indicator lamp control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted bulb driver.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to ground
Bulb driver internally shorted
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P263B.title: MIL Control Circuit High
P263B.description: Voltage on the malfunction indicator lamp control line is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open lamp.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to B+
Burnt-out MIL bulb
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P263C.title: Glow Plug Control Driver Performance
P263C.description: The glow plug control driver does not respond to commands within tolerance. Cold-start glow function is degraded so cold starting can be delayed and white smoke increases.

causes.label: Aged driver shows degraded switching behaviour
Current feedback loop noisy

symptoms: Glow plug warning light on (often orange coil symbol)
Hard cold start or no start in cold weather
White smoke from exhaust during warm-up

P263D.title: Reductant Heater Driver Performance
P263D.description: The reductant (AdBlue) tank or line heater driver does not switch as expected. AdBlue may freeze in cold weather, blocking SCR dosing.

causes.label: Aged driver shows degraded switching behaviour
Heater element resistance drifted out of range

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
AdBlue/DEF level or quality warning
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period
Failed emissions inspection (NOx)

P263E.title: Glow Plug Control Module 1 Over Temperature
P263E.description: The first glow plug control module reports over-temperature. Sustained current draw or insufficient cooling has driven the module above its rated temperature.

causes.label: One glow plug shorted to ground forces module overcurrent
Cooling air channel blocked by debris

symptoms: Glow plug warning light on (often orange coil symbol)
Hard cold start or no start in cold weather
White smoke from exhaust during warm-up

P263F.title: Glow Plug Control Module 2 Over Temperature
P263F.description: The second glow plug control module reports over-temperature. Sustained current draw or insufficient cooling has driven the module above its rated temperature.

causes.label: One glow plug shorted to ground forces module overcurrent
Cooling air channel blocked by debris

symptoms: Glow plug warning light on (often orange coil symbol)
Hard cold start or no start in cold weather
White smoke from exhaust during warm-up

P2640.title: Torque Management Feedback Signal A High
P2640.description: The torque feedback signal A reads above its valid range. Source module sends an implausibly high value or the bus signal is stuck high.

causes.label: Source module sends invalid high value
Signal stuck high on the bus

P2641.title: Torque Management Feedback Signal B
P2641.description: The torque feedback signal B from a second torque user is missing or invalid. The engine controller cannot coordinate torque reduction with this user.

causes.label: Required CAN message not received in time
Source module reports an internal fault

P2642.title: Torque Management Feedback Signal B Range/Performance
P2642.description: The torque feedback signal B is present but its value is implausible against measured engine load and speed. Sender calibration or sensor offset is suspected.

causes.label: Sender calibration drift
Bus value corrupted by EMI
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2643.title: Torque Management Feedback Signal B Low
P2643.description: The torque feedback signal B reads below its valid range. Source sends a value below physical possibility or the bus signal is stuck low.

causes.label: Source module sends invalid low value
Signal stuck low on the bus

P2644.title: Torque Management Feedback Signal B High
P2644.description: The torque feedback signal B reads above its valid range. Source sends an implausibly high value or the bus signal is stuck high.

causes.label: Source module sends invalid high value
Signal stuck high on the bus

P2645.title: A Rocker Arm Actuator Control Circuit / Open Bank 1
P2645.description: The controller cannot drive the rocker arm switching actuator A on bank 1 (used in cylinder deactivation systems such as VTEC, AFM, MDS). The valve lift mode cannot be switched.

causes.label: Open coil in oil control valve
Broken control wire

P2646.title: A Rocker Arm Actuator System Performance/Stuck Off Bank 1
P2646.description: The rocker arm actuator A on bank 1 is commanded to engage (high lift or all-cylinder mode) but does not switch. Engine stays in low-lift or deactivated mode under load, causing reduced power.

causes.label: Low oil pressure cannot move the actuator
Mechanical lock pin stuck in unactivated position
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2647.title: A Rocker Arm Actuator System Stuck On Bank 1
P2647.description: On variable valve lift systems (e.g. Honda VTEC) the ECU detects that the bank 1 rocker arm actuator is stuck in the engaged (high lift) position. Idle quality and fuel economy are affected.

causes.label: Insufficient oil pressure / level
Stuck VVL solenoid
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2648.title: A Rocker Arm Actuator Control Circuit Low Bank 1
P2648.description: Voltage on the rocker arm actuator A control line on bank 1 is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted solenoid coil.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in solenoid coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2649.title: A Rocker Arm Actuator Control Circuit High Bank 1
P2649.description: Voltage on the rocker arm actuator A control line on bank 1 is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open solenoid coil.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to B+
Open solenoid coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P264A.title: A Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Bank 1
P264A.description: The position sensor that confirms the A rocker arm switching state on bank 1 returns no usable signal. Closed-loop control of valve lift cannot verify the state.

causes.label: Open sensor element
Corroded sensor connector

P264B.title: A Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1
P264B.description: The position sensor reading does not transition cleanly between the two valve lift modes on bank 1. Sensor drift or mechanical wear leaves the signal between expected values.

causes.label: Sensor signal drift after thermal aging
Worn lock pin reduces travel between modes
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P264C.title: A Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Low Bank 1
P264C.description: The position sensor signal is below the lower diagnostic threshold. Usually a shorted sensor or short to ground in the harness.

causes.label: Internal short in sensor element
Signal wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P264D.title: A Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit High Bank 1
P264D.description: The position sensor signal is above the upper diagnostic threshold. Common causes are an open sensor or a short to the 5 V reference.

causes.label: Open sensor element
Signal wire shorted to the 5 V reference

Broken control wire to the pump

P26F5.title: Coolant Pump C Control Circuit Low
P26F5.description: Voltage on the third coolant pump control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted motor winding.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in pump motor winding
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26F6.title: Coolant Pump C Control Circuit High
P26F6.description: Voltage on the third coolant pump control line is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open motor winding.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to B+
Open motor winding
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P26F7.title: Coolant Pump C Supply Voltage Circuit
P26F7.description: The dedicated supply voltage line to the third coolant pump module is faulty. Pump cannot operate without battery feed.

causes.label: Blown fuse on supply line
High-resistance contact in supply harness

P26F8.title: Coolant Pump C Stuck/Stalled
P26F8.description: The third coolant pump is commanded on but the rotor does not turn. Sediment, frozen coolant, or a foreign object jams the impeller.

causes.label: Impeller jammed by sediment or debris
Pump motor seized by bearing failure

P26F9.title: Coolant Pump C Control Module Overtemperature
P26F9.description: The smart controller of the third coolant pump has reached over-temperature. Sustained high duty or insufficient cooling air flow around the pump electronics.

causes.label: Sustained high duty cycle from cooling demand
Cooling air channel around pump blocked by debris

P26FA.title: Coolant Pump C Overspeed/Air in System
P26FA.description: The third coolant pump speed feedback is higher than commanded with no resistance from coolant. Indicates air in the cooling loop or low coolant level so the pump spins free.

causes.label: Low coolant level due to leak or improper fill
Air pocket trapped in the cooling loop

P26FB.title: EGR Cooler Bypass Control Stuck Closed Bank 1
P26FB.description: The EGR cooler bypass valve on bank 1 is stuck in the closed position. EGR gas always passes through the cooler, which slows engine warm-up and can degrade cold-start emissions.

causes.label: Valve flap seized closed by soot
Actuator linkage jammed in closed position
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptoms: Check engine light on
Pinging or knocking under load
Power loss and hesitation
Possible rough idle
Failed emissions inspection (NOx)

P26FC.title: EGR Cooler Bypass Control Stuck Closed Bank 2
P26FC.description: The EGR cooler bypass valve on bank 2 is stuck in the closed position. EGR gas always passes through the cooler, slowing engine warm-up and degrading cold-start emissions.

causes.label: Valve flap seized closed by soot
Actuator linkage jammed in closed position
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptoms: Check engine light on
Pinging or knocking under load
Power loss and hesitation
Possible rough idle
Failed emissions inspection (NOx)

P26FD.title: A/C Compressor Internal Control Module Performance
P26FD.description: The internal control module of an electrically driven A/C compressor (typical on hybrid and BEV vehicles) reports an internal performance fault. Compressor capacity may be reduced or shut down.

causes.label: Internal fault in compressor inverter electronics
Software error in compressor control logic
Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

symptoms: Check engine light on
Possible limp mode or no-start
Multiple follow-up faults across modules
Reset/relearn may be needed after repair

P26FE.title: Exhaust Flow Control Valve A Control Performance
P26FE.description: The exhaust flow control valve A responds to commands but the resulting flow or back-pressure does not match expectations. Worn flap or carbon coking on the bore.

causes.label: Worn valve flap loses sealing
Carbon coking restricts valve travel

P26FF.title: Auto Configuration Throttle Input Not Present Bank 2
P26FF.description: During controller auto-configuration the expected throttle input on bank 2 was not detected. Configuration cannot complete and the second throttle path cannot be used.

causes.label: Broken signal wire from throttle B2
Hardware variant mismatch — sensor not installed
